text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- A five-member IMF delegation headed by its Middle East divisional chief Antonio Furtado arrived to review the economic measures taken by the government and to hold talks for the resumption of financial assistance to Pakistan.
- More than 96 percent of gross World Bank aid disbursement to Pakistan in 1996 will be consumed by repayment of principal and of interest and charges, according to a World Bank report.
- The government decided to cut road links between Islamabad and the rest of the country to foil Jamaat-i-Islami's planned sit-in in front of the Parliament House (lower house) on Sunday.
- All three Jamaat-i-Islami members of the National Assembly resigned their seats on the eve of party's march on the capital.
- All educational institutions, including colleges and schools, in the federal capital and federal territory will remain closed on Sunday.
- An effective and peaceful strike was observed in Karachi in protest against the imposition of new taxes, devaluation of the rupee and increase in petrol prices.
- The private software export board has received 40 proposals from 55 institutions worth at least 100 million rupees ($2.5 million) to set up industry-oriented computer centres.

- Eleven policemen allegedly involved in the September 20 shooting in which Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza Bhutto and seven of his aides were killed, were remanded in police custody on Saturday by the special court for the suppression of terrorist activities for 14 days.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- While the government struggles to obtain $80 million as the third tranche of the $600 million IMF loan, two foreign banks have just offered $130 million on soft terms to the state-run Trading Corp of Pakistan for trading operations.

- The government's efforts to get the early release of the $200 million Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd amortisation funds have failed as both Citibank and ABN-Amro have not signalled the disbursement date as yet.
- The external debt situation is so alarming now that it will need a national consensus on a long-term strategy to immediately reduce the burden of debt and debt-servicing.
- Pakistan has ordered expulsion within seven days of an under-cover Indian agent on charges of alleged espionage.
FINANCIAL POST

- Another round of rationalisation of the taxation system is expected to take place soon, following recommendations of the international donor agencies, aimed at redressing the grievances of taxpayers and improving internal revenue collection.
THE NEWS
- President Farooq Leghari will sign agreements on bilateral cooperation with Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev in Bishkek today.
- Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban movement has imposed a ban on opium poppy cultivation in areas it controls.
- Pakistan International Airlines has refused to collect central excise duty on concessionary domestic air tickets, arguing that this would adversely affect its business.
THE MUSLIM
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's mother Begum Nusrat Bhutto will soon take over as chairperson of the Pakistan People's Party to relieve part of her daughter's workload, insiders said.
-- Karachi newsroom 9221-5685192
